lines: Summary: Smuggling goods without customs procedures carries a penalty of 1-5 years, while selling or storing smuggled goods for commercial purposes carries a penalty of 1-3 years imprisonment. Attempted smuggling offenses are punished as completed offenses. However, if double the customs value of the goods is paid to the state, a half reduction in penalty is applied during the investigation phase, and a one-third reduction during the prosecution phase. Goods and transport vehicles used in smuggling are seized by the customs administration.

lines: Many tradesmen and importers believe that they cannot be held responsible for smuggling offenses unless they personally smuggle the goods across the border. However, Law No. 5607 punishes everyone involved in placing the goods into commercial circulation – buyers, sellers, transporters, storers – with the same seriousness. This lack of information can turn a well-intentioned supply error into a serious criminal investigation.

lines: Failure to subject commercial goods entering or leaving the country to legal customs procedures is considered not merely an administrative tax violation in our legal system, but a serious crime directly entailing custodial sentences. The primary regulation in this area is Law No. 5607 on Combating Smuggling. AI-supported risk analysis systems used in border controls have significantly increased the detection rate of these crimes in recent years.

lines: Article 3 of Law No. 5607 regulates in stages which acts constitute smuggling offenses according to the protected legal interest.

lines: Bringing Goods Without Customs Procedures (Art. 3/1): A person who brings goods into the country covertly or contrary to customs procedures at customs gates is subject to imprisonment from 1 to 5 years and a judicial fine of up to ten thousand days. If the goods are brought in from outside customs gates, for example, by illegal crossing of the border, the penalty is increased by half.

If the goods are brought in from outside customs gates, for example, by illegal crossing of the border, the penalty is increased by half.

lines: Selling, Transporting, or Storing Smuggled Goods for Commercial Purposes (Art. 3/10): This is the most common offense type affecting tradesmen, importers, and logistics companies in practice. A person who knowingly or needing to know that goods were smuggled into the country, purchases, offers for sale, transports, or stores them for commercial purposes is subject to imprisonment from 1 to 3 years and a judicial fine of up to five thousand days. For this offense to occur, the person does not need to have personally smuggled the goods across the border; it is sufficient for them to introduce the smuggled commodity into commercial circulation.

lines: Transit and Bonded Warehouse Regime Violations (Art. 3/5): In cases where goods declared for transit to another country or placed in bonded warehouses are diverted to the domestic market through fraudulent transactions to evade customs surveillance, the perpetrators are subject to imprisonment from 1 to 3 years.

lines: Critical Exception: Attempt Is Punished as a Completed Offense: According to the general provisions of the Turkish Penal Code, a penalty reduction is applied when an attempt is made to commit a crime. However, pursuant to the first paragraph of Article 4 of Law No. 5607, in smuggling offenses, an attempt is punished as a completed offense. Even if smuggled goods are caught at the border or at an airport exit, the crime is considered completed and a full penalty is imposed.

lines: Effective Repentance (Art. 5): A person involved in a smuggling offense can largely avoid imprisonment by paying double the customs value of the seized goods to the state treasury. If this payment is made during the investigation phase before a public lawsuit is filed, the penalty is reduced by half; if it is made after the lawsuit is filed but before a judgment is rendered, the penalty is reduced by one-third.

lines: Seizure of Goods and Transport Vehicles
5607-sayili-kanun-kacakcilik-suclari-reh.text: Seizure of Goods and Transport Vehicles

lines: Pursuant to Article 13 of Law No. 5607, all goods used in or constituting the subject of a smuggling offense, and the vehicles used for transporting these goods (trucks, lorries, ships, cars) are seized by the customs administration. For a transport vehicle to be confiscated, the smuggled goods must constitute a significant portion in terms of quantity and volume relative to the vehicle's load, or there must be specially prepared hidden compartments in the vehicle. For logistics companies to reclaim their vehicles, they must prove before the court that the driver was unaware of the smuggling act and that necessary corporate controls were performed, and deposit a certain guarantee of the vehicle's insurance value.

lines: How to Prepare a Consensual Divorce Protocol? Conditions and Critical Details Guide to Divorce in a Single Hearing Pursuant to Article 166/3 of the Turkish Civil Code. This guide has been updated based on the Turkish Civil Code and court practices in 2026.
anlasmali-bosanma-rehberi-ve-protokolu.text: How to Prepare a Consensual Divorce Protocol? Conditions and Critical Details Guide to Divorce in a Single Hearing Pursuant to Article 166/3 of the Turkish Civil Code. This guide has been updated based on the Turkish Civil Code and court practices in 2026.

lines: Summary Consensual divorce is a swift procedure to which spouses resort by reaching full agreement on the decision to divorce and all financial consequences. The law requires four conditions: the marriage must have lasted at least one year, the parties must apply together, the judge must personally hear both spouses in court, and the protocol must be approved by the judge. Drafting the provisions of the protocol regarding custody, alimony, compensation, and property division with clear, executable statements rather than ambiguous ones prevents new lawsuits from being filed in the future.

lines: Consensual divorce is known as the type of divorce where spouses separate with the least resentment and which concludes the fastest. However, this speed does not mean that the protocol can be prepared carelessly. Even if the hearing ends in one day, the signed protocol becomes a court order binding on the parties for years. A sentence like "Alimony shall be paid as much as the circumstances permit" can tie the hands of the enforcement office tomorrow.

lines: Four Legal Conditions for Consensual Divorce
anlasmali-bosanma-rehberi-ve-protokolu.text: Four Legal Conditions for Consensual Divorce

lines: Consensual divorce is regulated under the third paragraph of Article 166 of the Turkish Civil Code. The mere agreement between the parties is not sufficient; the following four conditions must be met concurrently.
anlasmali-bosanma-rehberi-ve-protokolu.text: Consensual divorce is regulated under the third paragraph of Article 166 of the Turkish Civil Code. The mere agreement between the parties is not sufficient; the following four conditions must be met concurrently.

lines: The marriage must have lasted at least one year: A full year (365 days) must have passed from the date of the official marriage registration until the day the lawsuit is filed. Engagement periods or cohabitation periods are not included in this calculation. Lawsuits filed before the period expires will be rejected, even if the parties agree. Joint application or acceptance: Spouses must apply to the court with a joint petition and protocol, or in a lawsuit filed by one spouse, the other spouse must accept all conditions unconditionally during the hearing. The judge must personally hear the parties: Even if they have lawyers, both spouses must be personally present in court on the day of the hearing. The judge wants to personally see and hear that the parties have expressed their will without coercion or deception. It is invalid for a lawyer to declare the intention to divorce on behalf of their client with a power of attorney. Approval of the protocol by the judge: The submitted protocol is reviewed by the judge. If the judge perceives a situation contrary to the child's best interest, especially concerning child custody and personal relationship arrangements, they can intervene in the protocol. If the parties accept the change, the divorce takes place; if they do not accept, the case turns into a contested divorce.

lines: Mr. Ahmet (engineer) and Ms. Elif (teacher) have been officially married for 4 years and have a 3-year-old child named Mert. Realizing that they cannot continue their marriage due to differences of opinion, they have agreed on all conditions and prepared a consensual divorce protocol.
anlasmali-bosanma-rehberi-ve-protokolu.text: Mr. Ahmet (engineer) and Ms. Elif (teacher) have been officially married for 4 years and have a 3-year-old child named Mert. Realizing that they cannot continue their marriage due to differences of opinion, they have agreed on all conditions and prepared a consensual divorce protocol.

lines: Shaping of the Protocol Considering the child's age, custody was granted to Ms. Elif. It was decided that Mr. Ahmet would have personal contact with the child every second weekend of the month and during the summer holidays from July 1-15. Mr. Ahmet agreed to pay 15,000 TL per month as child support, with an annual increase at the CPI rate in January each year included in the article. Since Ms. Elif had a regular income, no spousal support was requested, and the parties mutually waived their rights to compensation. The family home remained with Ms. Elif, and the vehicle remained with Mr. Ahmet.

lines: Trial and Outcome
anlasmali-bosanma-rehberi-ve-protokolu.text: Trial and Outcome

lines: The protocol, wet-signed, was submitted to the court, and both parties were personally present on the hearing day. The judge, after hearing the free will of the parties and verifying that the protocol was in the child's best interest, granted a divorce in a single hearing. The parties submitted a waiver of appeal, finalizing the process within 35 days.

lines: Frequently Asked Questions
anlasmali-bosanma-rehberi-ve-protokolu.text: Frequently Asked Questions

lines: Can the protocol be abandoned until the decision becomes final? Yes. According to the established jurisprudence of the Supreme Court, even if the judge has rendered a judgment, the spouses have the right to withdraw from their intention to divorce or from the terms of the protocol until the decision officially becomes final. If one of the parties objects, the case is converted by the court into a contested divorce case and proceeds from the beginning with an investigation procedure.

lines: Can penal clauses such as "pays compensation if remarries" be included in the protocol? No. It is essential that the protocol provisions do not violate public order, personal rights, and mandatory legal provisions. Clauses restricting the freedom to remarry or conditioning the divorce decision will not be accepted by the judge and will lead to the correction of the protocol.

lines: What happens if property division or jewelry is not written in the protocol? To be able to divorce consensually, it is mandatory to agree on custody, child support, spousal support, and compensation; the liquidation of the matrimonial property regime and wedding jewelry are not mandatory elements. If there is no clause or general waiver statement on these issues in the protocol, the right to file a separate lawsuit for the liquidation of the matrimonial property regime or a lawsuit for jewelry within the 10-year statute of limitations after the divorce remains reserved. However, to avoid dealing with a new lawsuit later, it is the healthiest way to resolve these issues in the protocol.

lines: Attention: Common Mistakes in Protocols
anlasmali-bosanma-rehberi-ve-protokolu.text: Attention: Common Mistakes in Protocols

lines: Ambiguous statements: Vague clauses such as "personal relationship with the child can be established at any time" or "alimony shall be paid as much as the circumstances permit" prevent the enforcement of this document, which has the nature of a judgment; if alimony is not paid, the enforcement office cannot pursue it without a clear amount. Missing title deed transfer clause: The statement "The immovable property will be transferred to Elif's name" is not sufficient. The transfer period, the relevant land registry office, island-parcel information, and that the judgment will be enforceable for registration if not transferred, must also be explicitly stated. Otherwise, if a spouse avoids the transfer, a new lawsuit that could last for years might be necessary.

lines: Conclusion
anlasmali-bosanma-rehberi-ve-protokolu.text: Conclusion

lines: A consensual divorce offers parties a fast and less burdensome solution with a properly prepared protocol. However, this speed depends on every provision of the protocol being executable, clear, and compliant with the law. A small omission in the provisions regarding custody, alimony, compensation, and property division can mean knocking on the courthouse door again years later.

lines: Banking and Finance Law
banka-hesabina-konulan-haksiz-bloke-rehb.text: Banking and Finance Law

lines: Summary: A freeze placed on a bank account may result from the bank's internal risk decision, MASAK's administrative suspension authority under Article 19/A of Law No. 5549, or a judicial seizure measure under Articles 128 and 128/A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CMK) applied by the Public Prosecutor's Office and the Criminal Judgeship of Peace. The legal basis, duration, and appeal authority for these three types of freezes are entirely different; an appeal not made to the correct authority within the correct timeframe can leave the account holder unable to access their money for months.

lines: The Same Word, Three Different Legal Paths: "Freeze " Whose Decision?
banka-hesabina-konulan-haksiz-bloke-rehb.text: The Same Word, Three Different Legal Paths: "Freeze " Whose Decision?

lines: While a notification from a bank stating "your account has been frozen" is often summarized with the same phrase, it conceals one of three entirely different legal mechanisms. Confusing whether it is the bank's own decision, an administrative measure by MASAK, or a judicial seizure order by the prosecutor's office leads to appeals being submitted to the wrong authority and weeks of lost time.

lines: This guide addresses how to distinguish between types of freezes, to which authority and within what timeframe an appeal should be made, and the current legislation as of 2026.

lines: Legal Grounds for Freezing a Bank Account
banka-hesabina-konulan-haksiz-bloke-rehb.text: Legal Grounds for Freezing a Bank Account

lines: A bank account freeze is not based on a single legal cause. The most frequently encountered types of freezes in practice are; attachments originating from enforcement or tax offices, administrative freezes imposed by the bank based on its own suspicious transaction risk policy, MASAK's suspension decision under Law No. 5549, and judicial seizure measures under the Code of Criminal Procedure (CMK) applied by the Public Prosecutor's Office or the Criminal Judgeship of Peace. Especially in accounts associated with illegal betting, crypto asset transactions, and suspected fraud, MASAK and prosecutor's office freezes are applied in an intertwined manner; therefore, the first step to take is to identify which authority placed the freeze and on what grounds.

Especially in accounts associated with illegal betting, crypto asset transactions, and suspected fraud, MASAK and prosecutor's office freezes are applied in an intertwined manner; therefore, the first step to take is to identify which authority placed the freeze and on what grounds.

lines: Correctly identifying the source of the freeze determines the legal course of action to be followed. A written application should be made to the bank requesting "the name of the authority that imposed the freeze, the file number, and details of the underlying warrant"; appeal petitions prepared without obtaining this information carry the risk of being submitted to the wrong authority.

lines: MASAK Freeze
banka-hesabina-konulan-haksiz-bloke-rehb.text: MASAK Freeze

lines: The Financial Crimes Investigation Board (MASAK) has the authority to suspend a transaction for a period of 7 business days if there is suspicion that the transaction is linked to money laundering or terrorist financing. Although this period is clearly defined in the law, in practice, it can extend to between 15 and 60 days due to caseload intensity. If no strong suspicion is found at the end of the review, the freeze is lifted ex officio; if suspicion persists, the file is transferred to the Public Prosecutor's Office, and the process turns into a judicial measure.

lines: Prosecutor's Office / Criminal Judgeship of Peace Freeze
banka-hesabina-konulan-haksiz-bloke-rehb.text: Prosecutor's Office / Criminal Judgeship of Peace Freeze

lines: If suspicion that the account is linked to a crime intensifies as a result of a MASAK investigation, the Public Prosecutor requests the Criminal Judgeship of Peace to seize the amount in the account in accordance with Article 128 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In cases where delay is inconvenient, the prosecutor's office may issue a direct seizure order; however, this decision must be submitted for the judge's approval within 24 hours. From this stage onwards, the freeze becomes part of the criminal investigation, and its removal is only possible with a decision from the relevant Criminal Judgeship of Peace.

lines: New Regime: Article 128/A of the CMK, added to the Code of Criminal Procedure by Article 22 of Law No. 7571 and effective from December 25, 2025, grants banks and crypto asset service providers the authority to ex officio suspend an account for up to 48 hours, especially in cases related to IT crimes and crypto asset transactions. Within this period, the prosecutor can issue a seizure order by written instruction; if the judge does not approve within 48 hours from the seizure, the measure automatically lapses. Under the old regime, it took 5 days for the prosecutor's decision to be submitted to the judge and 10 days for the judge to rule; under the new regime, these periods have been reduced to 24+24 hours; this is a procedural point that must be checked in appeal petitions.

lines: Procedure to Follow for Lifting a Freeze
banka-hesabina-konulan-haksiz-bloke-rehb.text: Procedure to Follow for Lifting a Freeze

lines: Firstly, the authority that placed the freeze, the underlying warrant, and the file number, if any, should be requested from the bank in writing. Then, for a MASAK freeze, a petition requesting "the lifting of the freeze and the issuance of a warrant to the bank" is submitted to the MASAK Presidency; for a freeze under the prosecutor's office or CMK, it is submitted to the relevant Criminal Judgeship of Peace. In this petition, the legitimate source of the money must be proven with documents such as salary statements, invoices, contracts, title deeds, or bank receipts.

lines: If the entire account has been frozen while the suspicious transaction amount is low, it may be requested that the freeze be limited only to the suspicious amount, based on the principle of proportionality. Compliance with the 48+48 hour approval periods stipulated under CMK Art. 128/A should also be checked; it should be argued that a measure for which judge's approval was not obtained within the period automatically becomes void. If no result is achieved, an annulment lawsuit can be filed in the Administrative Court against MASAK's administrative decision, and a compensation lawsuit can be filed under CMK Art. 141 for damages incurred due to unlawful seizure.

lines: Mr. Kerem, an architect, received a notification from his bank stating "your account has been frozen by MASAK instruction" after receiving a 180,000 TL transfer into his account from a relative living abroad for project consultancy. On the same day, automatic payments linked to his salary account also became inoperable.

lines: Litigation and Proof Process
banka-hesabina-konulan-haksiz-bloke-rehb.text: Litigation and Proof Process

lines: Mr. Kerem's lawyer first requested the basis of the freeze from the bank in writing, and it was determined that the freeze was an administrative measure imposed by MASAK. An appeal petition proving the legitimacy of the fund's source was submitted to the MASAK Presidency, accompanied by the consultancy agreement, correspondence with his relative, his relative's overseas bank statement, and self-employment receipts related to his architectural activities. The petition also emphasized that freezing the entire account due to a single transaction was disproportionate.

lines: I can't even withdraw my salary, what should I do? First, it should be learned in writing from the bank whether the freeze is an internal bank decision, a MASAK decision, or a prosecutor's decision. For vital payments such as salaries, it is possible to request partial withdrawal permission from the court or MASAK. Making this request with a petition supported by concrete documents increases the likelihood of a positive outcome.

lines: MASAK freeze says 7 business days, but my account has been frozen for 2 months, isn't this illegal? The 7-business-day period in the law is the target period for MASAK to complete its administrative review; in practice, this period may actually be exceeded due to caseload intensity. Exceeding the period alone does not mean the freeze is unlawful, but an appeal can be made to MASAK and, if necessary, to the Administrative Court on the grounds of violating the principle of reasonable time.

lines: The freeze has been lifted, but I suffered damages during this process, can I get compensation? Persons who have suffered damages due to an unlawfully applied seizure can file a compensation lawsuit against the state under Article 141 et seq. of the CMK. For such a lawsuit to be filed, the unlawfulness of the measure and the damage must be concretely proven; in cases of damages related to MASAK's administrative decision, the remedy of filing a full remedy lawsuit in the Administrative Court is considered.

lines: Summary In Turkey, unless couples agree otherwise, they are subject to the "Regime of Participation in Acquired Property"; under this regime, half of all assets acquired through work during marriage are the right of the other spouse upon divorce. Personal property is excluded from this division. Wedding jewelry, unless proven otherwise, is considered the wife's personal property and can be reclaimed even if spent on household expenses. Procedural tools such as preliminary injunctions and actions for annulment of disposition are available against attempts to conceal assets.

lines: One of the most common misconceptions in divorce proceedings is the belief that ownership of a title deed or invoice determines who owns that property. This is not how it works in Turkish law. Even if an apartment bought during marriage was purchased with the husband's salary and registered solely in his name, the wife acquires a right to half of that value. Below, the source and limits of this right and specific rules for wedding jewelry are discussed.

lines: Regime of Participation in Acquired Property: What Property is Subject to Division?
bosanmada-mal-paylasimi-ve-ziynet-rehber.text: Regime of Participation in Acquired Property: What Property is Subject to Division?

lines: Pursuant to the Turkish Civil Code which came into force on January 1, 2002, if spouses have not signed a contrary property regime contract when marrying, the "Regime of Participation in Acquired Property" legally applies between them. Under this regime, in the event of divorce, each spouse has a fifty percent right to the assets acquired through their own labor during the marriage. For correct division, the law divides property into two categories.
bosanmada-mal-paylasimi-ve-ziynet-rehber.text: Pursuant to the Turkish Civil Code which came into force on January 1, 2002, if spouses have not signed a contrary property regime contract when marrying, the "Regime of Participation in Acquired Property" legally applies between them. Under this regime, in the event of divorce, each spouse has a fifty percent right to the assets acquired through their own labor during the marriage. For correct division, the law divides property into two categories.

lines: Acquired Property (Subject to Division) Acquisitions in return for work: Income from salary, bonuses, freelance earnings, or commercial enterprises of one spouse during marriage. Social security payments: The portion of retirement bonuses, severance pay, disability pensions, or temporary incapacity benefits corresponding to the duration of the marriage. Income from personal property: Rental income from a property owned before marriage or interest income accrued on personal money during marriage is considered acquired property pursuant to Article 219, paragraph four of the Turkish Civil Code. Values replacing acquired property: If a vehicle bought with money earned during marriage is sold and real estate is purchased in its place, that real estate also has the status of acquired property.

Values replacing acquired property: If a vehicle bought with money earned during marriage is sold and real estate is purchased in its place, that real estate also has the status of acquired property.

lines: Personal Property (Not Subject to Division) Pre-marital assets: Movable and immovable assets acquired by one spouse with their savings or with family support before marriage. Inheritance and gratuitous acquisitions: Even if during marriage, inheritance left to one spouse by their family or direct donations made to them (including lottery winnings). Claims for non-pecuniary damages: Amounts of non-pecuniary damages awarded to one spouse in their own name due to an injustice suffered. Personal use items: Items exclusively for one spouse's use, such as personal clothing, professional tools, or a personal computer. Division of Wedding Jewelry: Who Owns It?

lines: Wedding jewelry is one of the areas where clients most frequently suffer loss of rights in field cases. According to the settled jurisprudence of the General Assembly of Civil Chambers of the Supreme Court, wedding jewelry (gold, bracelets, sets, money), regardless of type and to whom it was given, is considered the personal property of the wife, unless there is contrary custom, tradition, or written agreement.

lines: Regarding cash or quarter gold coins given to the husband, which are not specific to women, if there is no strong local custom indicating that the jewelry belongs to the woman, her right is protected. To claim jewelry in a divorce case, a separate lawsuit for jewelry claims must be filed, and the existence of the jewelry must be concretely proven through wedding videos, photographs, or expert examination.

lines: The most common defense in practice is the claim that the jewelry was cashed in to pay wedding debts or for a down payment on a house. In this situation, the Supreme Court holds the male spouse responsible: unless the female spouse explicitly states that she "donated the gold, never to be taken back" when it was cashed in and used for a debt, the male spouse is obliged to return the value of this jewelry to the woman in kind or in cash. If it was used for the purchase of a house or car, the woman's right arising from this amount is included in the property division case as a "claim for increased value share."

lines: Ms. Meltem and Mr. Hakan married in 2015, filed for divorce in 2024, and their marriage ended with a final decision in 2026. During the marriage, an apartment was purchased with Mr. Hakan's engineering salary and registered in his name in the title deed. At the wedding, Ms. Meltem was given 20 Cumhuriyet gold coins and 5 bracelets; these gold coins were cashed in during the marriage and used for the down payment on the apartment. Mr. Hakan objected to the claim, asserting that the house was bought with his salary and the title deed was in his name.

lines: Trial and Proof Process In the property regime liquidation and jewelry claim lawsuit filed by Ms. Meltem through her attorney at the Antalya Family Court, a preliminary injunction was first placed on the title deed to prevent the apartment from being sold to third parties. Wedding videos were examined by an expert to determine the list of gold coins given to Ms. Meltem and their current market value. The court determined that the gold coins were used for the apartment's down payment and calculated this amount as a claim for increased value share in favor of Ms. Meltem.

lines: Legal Ruling In line with the expert report, the court ruled that 1,800,000 TL, comprising the liquidation share claim, which is half of the current value of the apartment, and the cash equivalent of the wedding jewelry spent on the down payment, should be collected from Mr. Hakan and paid to Ms. Meltem. Mr. Hakan's defense that the house was "bought with his own salary" was rejected because the salary acquired during marriage is legally considered acquired property.

lines: Does rent income from a house purchased before marriage, acquired during marriage, enter into property division? Yes. Pursuant to Article 219, paragraph four of the Turkish Civil Code, rental, interest, or dividend income generated by one spouse's personal property during marriage is considered acquired property. These accumulated incomes during marriage, or new assets purchased with this income, are subject to fifty-fifty division upon divorce.
bosanmada-mal-paylasimi-ve-ziynet-rehber.text: Does rent income from a house purchased before marriage, acquired during marriage, enter into property division? Yes. Pursuant to Article 219, paragraph four of the Turkish Civil Code, rental, interest, or dividend income generated by one spouse's personal property during marriage is considered acquired property. These accumulated incomes during marriage, or new assets purchased with this income, are subject to fifty-fifty division upon divorce.

lines: How do loans taken by a spouse during marriage affect property division? In property liquidation, each spouse's debts related to acquired property are deducted from the value of that property. For example, if a car purchased with a loan still has outstanding loan debt at the date of the divorce lawsuit, the remaining debt is deducted from the market value of the car, and the division is made over the net remaining amount. However, a spouse's personal debts, gambling debts, or secret debts unrelated to the family do not bind the other spouse.

lines: The spouse transferred their assets to relatives before the lawsuit was filed; what can be done? This is the most common method of asset concealment encountered in practice. Pursuant to Article 229 of the Turkish Civil Code, gratuitous dispositions made by one spouse within one year prior to the divorce lawsuit without the other spouse's consent, with the aim of reducing the rights arising from liquidation, are calculated by adding them to the existing assets as if they had never been transferred. A lawsuit for the annulment of disposition can be filed against third parties for the annulment of these fraudulent sales.

lines: Failure to clearly state the claim in the petition: Failure to additionally and clearly specify the request for liquidation of the property regime and the jewelry claim in the divorce petition leads to insufficient court fees and failure to itemize the assets. A divorce case and a property division case are two entirely independent actions in terms of fees and procedure.

lines: Incorrect valuation date: The value of real estate or vehicles is not calculated based on the date the divorce case was filed, but rather on the current market value at the liquidation date closest to the court's decision. Prolonging the case means that the value of the property increases in an inflationary environment; therefore, timely objections to expert reports or requesting additional reports is crucial.

lines: Summary A contested divorce lawsuit is a type of lawsuit where spouses cannot agree on the decision to end the marriage or on secondary issues such as custody, alimony, and division of property, and the court independently investigates the claims. For a divorce decision to be rendered, at least one of the grounds listed in the law must be proven with concrete evidence. The lawsuit proceeds through five procedural stages: exchange of petitions, preliminary examination, investigation, oral hearing, and decision; the first instance process takes an average of 18-36 months, and finalization, including appeal and cassation, can take 4-5 years.

lines: A contested divorce lawsuit is filed when spouses cannot agree on the decision to end the marriage or on financial and legal consequences dependent on divorce, such as custody, alimony, and property division. Unlike an uncontested divorce, there is a conflict of interest between the parties here, and the court independently investigates the veracity of the claims.

lines: The Turkish Civil Code divides grounds for divorce into general and specific grounds. These grounds are also classified as absolute and relative grounds. In absolute grounds, proving the action alone is sufficient for a divorce decision; in relative grounds, in addition to the action, it is also investigated whether common life has become unbearable for the other spouse.

lines: General Grounds for Divorce The first and second paragraphs of Article 166 of the Turkish Civil Code regulate the breakdown of the marital union. This is the article with the broadest application area in the law: the collapse of the intellectual, spiritual, and physical foundations of the marital relationship, and the disappearance of the minimum bond of respect and affection between the parties. Persistent insults, tendencies to physical violence, serious injustices against the spouse's family, intentionally causing economic hardship to the family, and actions that undermine trust are the main elements of this article.

lines: The fourth paragraph of the same article regulates a separate possibility: if a divorce lawsuit filed for any reason is rejected and three years pass from the finalization of the decision, and common life has not been re-established, the marital union is deemed to have broken down fundamentally, and divorce is directly decreed upon the request of one of the spouses. This is an absolute ground.

lines: Specific Grounds for Divorce Adultery (Turkish Civil Code art.161): One of the spouses engaging in sexual intercourse with a third person with consent while the marriage persists. This is an absolute ground; it is subject to forfeiture periods of 6 months from discovery and 5 years from the act. Hotel records, bank statements, photographs, and messages are the most common means of proof. Attempted murder, severe ill-treatment, or disgraceful conduct (art.162): Attacks on the spouse's right to life, acts of torture and severe beating, or serious attacks targeting a person's honor and dignity are evaluated within this scope. Committing a crime and leading a dishonorable life (art.163): Committing a humiliating crime that damages the other spouse's position in society or persistently leading a dishonorable lifestyle such as gambling addiction or prostitution. Desertion (art.164): Filed against a spouse who leaves the common residence or does not return without a justifiable reason to avoid fulfilling marital obligations. The separation must have lasted at least 6 months, and a proper warning to return must have been issued through the court or notary. Mental illness (art.165): One of the spouses suffering from a mental illness, confirmed by an official health board report as incurable, and this condition making common life unbearable for the other spouse. This is a relative ground; the condition of unbearableness is absolutely required.

This is a relative ground; the condition of unbearableness is absolutely required.

lines: The process can be evaluated in three stages. The first instance stage, meaning the process in the family court, takes an average of 18 to 36 months; in courthouses in metropolitan areas, this period approaches the upper limit due to workload. The intensity of appointments for experts such as pedagogues, psychologists, and social workers, and the report preparation times, can cause hearing intervals to extend up to 4-6 months; witnesses not being present on the hearing day is another factor that prolongs the process.

lines: Can a contested lawsuit later turn into an uncontested one? Yes. At any stage of the proceedings, even before a judgment is rendered and the file goes to appeal, the parties can come together and sign an uncontested divorce protocol. In this case, the court can bring forward the hearing date, hear the parties, and conclude the case in a single session; this saves significant time.

lines: When do temporary alimony and custody measures come into play? Pursuant to Article 169 of the Turkish Civil Code, upon the filing of a lawsuit, the judge automatically takes necessary temporary measures regarding the housing, subsistence, management of property, and care of children of the spouses during the continuation of the lawsuit. In this context, provisional custody and provisional alimony are decided at the beginning of the lawsuit and applied until the case is concluded.

lines: How are wedding gifts (jewelry) evaluated in a contested case? According to the established jurisprudence of the General Assembly of the Court of Cassation, wedding jewelry, regardless of its type and who it was given to, is considered the personal property of the woman unless there is a contrary custom or written agreement. If the male spouse claims that the jewelry should remain with him, he is obliged to prove this.

lines: Press and Media Law
cevap-ve-duzeltme-tekzip-hakki-rehberi.text: Press and Media Law

lines: Summary The right of reply and correction (retraction) is the authority of an individual or institution to have their statement published in the same medium against an untrue publication made about them. In the written press, the application period is 2 months from the date of publication and must be made through a notary; the responsible manager is obliged to publish this text in the daily publication within 3 days. In internet media, the text must be published within 24 hours of the application and for at least 1 week. If not published, an application can be made to the Criminal Judgeship of Peace within 15 days.

lines: It's Not Enough to Say a Baseless News is "False"; Correct Procedure is Required

lines: The first reaction of a person or institution about whom an untrue news item has been published is usually to make a statement on social media. However, the legal system offers a much more powerful tool to deliver accurate information to the same audience through the same medium: the right of retraction. The power of this right comes from its ability to compel the media outlet to publish even by judicial decision, when used correctly; however, the time and formal rules are quite strict.

lines: What is the Right of Reply and Correction?
cevap-ve-duzeltme-tekzip-hakki-rehberi.text: What is the Right of Reply and Correction?

lines: The right of reply and correction is the authority of an individual or institution to have their statement published as is in the relevant media outlet within legal timeframes, against a radio, television, newspaper, magazine, or internet publication that is untrue or damages their personal rights. This right is regulated in Article 32 of the Constitution of the Republic of Turkey; according to the Constitution, this right is recognized in cases where a person's honor and dignity are touched upon or untrue publications are made about them. Its application in the written press is detailed in Article 14 of Press Law No. 5187.

lines: Conditions for the Right of Retraction
cevap-ve-duzeltme-tekzip-hakki-rehberi.text: Conditions for the Right of Retraction

lines: For the right of retraction to arise against a publication, the legislation requires three conditions to be met collectively. Merely disliking a news item or finding it critical does not give rise to the right of retraction.
cevap-ve-duzeltme-tekzip-hakki-rehberi.text: For the right of retraction to arise against a publication, the legislation requires three conditions to be met collectively. Merely disliking a news item or finding it critical does not give rise to the right of retraction.

lines: Violation of personal rights: The publication must contain elements that damage the honor, dignity, commercial reputation, or professional integrity of the person or institution. Untruthfulness: The claims in the publication must not be consistent with concrete reality, be baseless, or create a false perception by being presented incompletely. Direct relevance: The name of the person whose right has been violated must be clearly mentioned in the publication, or if no name is given, it must be understood without doubt by the public who this person is.

lines: Retraction Process in Written Press
cevap-ve-duzeltme-tekzip-hakki-rehberi.text: Retraction Process in Written Press

lines: The person whose rights have been violated must deliver the reply and correction text to the responsible manager of the relevant publication within 2 months from the date of the untrue publication. For proof purposes, it is important that this submission is made through a notary in the form of a notice to prevent loss of rights. The responsible manager is obliged to publish the text within 3 days in daily periodicals, and in the first issue following the receipt of the text in other periodicals. The retraction text must be published exactly as is, on the page where the allegations appeared, in the same columns, in the same font, and without any added comments.

lines: Judicial Remedy in Case of Rejection of the Request
cevap-ve-duzeltme-tekzip-hakki-rehberi.text: Judicial Remedy in Case of Rejection of the Request

lines: If the responsible manager of the media outlet fails to publish the retraction text, publishes it late, or publishes it in violation of formal requirements (e.g., in a small font or on a back page), the process is taken to court. The victim can apply to the Criminal Judgeship of Peace in their place of residence or where the media outlet's headquarters are located, within 15 days from the end of the publication period, requesting the publication of the text by court order. The judge examines the request over documents without holding a hearing and makes a final decision within 3 days at the latest. If the decision is favorable, it is notified to the Association of Access Providers or directly to the publication body; severe administrative fines are imposed on responsible managers who fail to publish the text despite the final decision.

lines: Can I write anything I want in the retraction text? No. The text cannot contain expressions that are insulting, threatening, or violate the rights of third parties, and it should not exceed the volume of the article that caused the violation; in written press, it is generally expected not to exceed 300 words. The presence of criminal elements in the text or exceeding the length limit leads to the direct rejection of the request by the Criminal Judgeship of Peace.

lines: Can I directly apply to the judgeship without sending a notarized warning? No. First, an application must be made to the publication body or responsible manager within the legal period, and only if this application is rejected or not published within the time limit can an application be made to the judgeship. A judgeship application cannot be evaluated without a document showing that the initial application was made.

lines: Summary: If ornamental gold brought from abroad does not exceed 15,000 USD, it can be brought in without declaration; however, bringing in gold bars or amounts exceeding this limit by concealment constitutes a smuggling offense under Law No. 5607. The mobile phone exemption is 1 per 3 years; additional phones may be considered commercial and confiscated. The exemption limit for luxury goods is 430 Euros; personal items exceeding this limit must be declared and taxed, attempts to conceal them may result in an administrative fine or a judicial investigation if the quantity is commercial.

lines: With the increase in international travel, the tendency to bring in gold, smartphones, and luxury brand items is also rising. AI-powered x-ray scans and physical inspections at airports are detecting these items much more frequently than before. The widespread public belief that "if caught, only the item is confiscated" is incomplete information. Depending on the nature, method, and quantity of the item, the process can escalate directly to a heavy penal trial with a demand for imprisonment.

lines: Two different laws come into play when gold is brought into Turkey from abroad, and the line between them is thin enough to carry the risk of imprisonment.
gumruk-altin-telefon-luks-esya-kacakcili.text: Two different laws come into play when gold is brought into Turkey from abroad, and the line between them is thin enough to carry the risk of imprisonment.

lines: Pursuant to Decision No. 32 on the Protection of the Value of Turkish Currency, travelers can bring personal ornamental gold into Turkey without declaration, provided it is not for commercial purposes and its value does not exceed 15,000 US Dollars. It is mandatory to declare ornamental gold exceeding this amount at customs entry.

It is mandatory to declare ornamental gold exceeding this amount at customs entry.

lines: The biggest misconception here is the assumption that bullion, bars, or investment gold can also be freely brought in under traveler's exemption. Investment gold is subject to a special import regime and cannot be brought in tax-free or without declaration by travelers. If a traveler is caught attempting to pass through the Green Channel with ornamental gold above the legal limit or any quantity of bullion gold, regardless of amount, for the purpose of evading customs control (by concealing it in a pocket, hiding it at the bottom of a suitcase, or wrapping it around the body), this action constitutes a customs smuggling offense under the first paragraph of Article 3 of Law No. 5607, not a simple violation of regulations.

lines: The limit for mobile phones that travelers can bring from abroad tax-free and exempt is only 1 per 3 calendar years. It is mandatory to register this phone to the traveler's passport and use it with a line registered to their ID number. If a traveler carries more than one boxed, new phone in their luggage exceeding this limit and attempts to pass through the Green Channel without declaring it, customs officials will consider the additional phones as commercial goods. If the phones are concealed in an unusual manner or their number is indicative of commercial gain, a smuggling investigation will be initiated under Law No. 5607, and all phones will be confiscated.

lines: Exemption Limit for Luxury Bags, Watches, and Clothing The exemption limit for personal luxury items brought by travelers, not of commercial quantity or nature, is set at a total of 430 Euros (150 Euros for those under 15 years old). For a luxury watch or bag exceeding this value, the traveler must go through the Red Channel, declare the item, and pay customs duty (approximately 20-30%) for the exceeding portion.

lines: If a traveler attempts to pass through the Green Channel with luxury items worth thousands of Euros by removing them from their boxes, wearing them, removing their labels, and presenting them as personal belongings, and is caught, the customs administration will detect the fraudulent act. If the quantity is within personal consumption limits, an administrative fine of twice the taxes will be imposed according to the third paragraph of Article 235 of Customs Law No. 4458. If there is more than one of the same product and it is determined to be brought for commercial purposes, judicial proceedings will be initiated directly under Law No. 5607.

lines: The form of the gold as bullion and its concealment in the jacket lining indicate an intention to fraudulently circumvent customs control. The customs directorate filed a criminal complaint with the judicial authorities; a public prosecution was initiated against Mr. Serkan for 1 to 5 years of imprisonment under the first paragraph of Article 3 of Law No. 5607, and the court confiscated the gold, which had a high market value.

lines: If I am bringing the products as gifts for relatives, do the limits still apply? Yes. Customs legislation also limits the concept of "gift" with legal exemption limits. For example, finding 4 phones with unopened boxes and 3 luxury bags in luggage, even if claimed for gifting purposes, can be considered commercial quantity and may lead to a smuggling investigation beyond an administrative penalty.

As soon as a smuggling report is drawn up, the process becomes judicial; it is important to seek support from a lawyer before making a statement.

lines: Attention: Common Mistakes Made During the Process Choosing the wrong channel: Attempting to pass through the Green Channel with an item that should be declared can, by itself, turn an administrative violation into a suspicion of smuggling. Missing objection periods: There is a right to object to administrative monetary penalties with the customs administration within 15 days from the notification; if this period is missed, the penalty becomes final.

lines: Summary Lawsuits cannot be filed directly with the tax court against customs duties and administrative fines; it is first mandatory to object to the Regional Customs Directorate within 15 days from the notification date. If the administration does not respond within 30 days, the objection is deemed implicitly rejected. An annulment lawsuit can be filed with the Tax Court within 30 days from the notification of the rejection decision or the expiry of the implicit rejection period. These periods are peremptory; a delay of even one day leads to the finalization of the action.

lines: Mandatory Administrative Objection Stage
gumruk-vergisi-ve-para-cezalarina-itiraz.text: Mandatory Administrative Objection Stage

lines: The most characteristic feature of customs legislation is that lawsuits cannot be filed directly with the tax court against customs duties and administrative fines. Pursuant to Article 242 of Customs Law No. 4458, the mandatory administrative objection route must be exhausted before resorting to judicial remedies. Lawsuits filed directly, bypassing this stage, are procedurally dismissed by the court with a decision to send the petition to the administrative authority.

Pursuant to Article 242 of Customs Law No. 4458, the mandatory administrative objection route must be exhausted before resorting to judicial remedies. Lawsuits filed directly, bypassing this stage, are procedurally dismissed by the court with a decision to send the petition to the administrative authority.

lines: Obligors must object to the Regional Customs Directorate, to which the customs directorate that issued the decision is affiliated, with a reasoned petition within 15 days from the date of notification of the customs duty, additional assessment, and administrative fines notified to them. This period is peremptory; if missed, the administrative action becomes final and cannot be litigated again.

lines: The Regional Customs Directorate receiving the objection is obliged to make a decision within 30 days. There are three possibilities: the administration may accept the error and annul the action, reject the objection, or not respond at all within the period. If no response is given within thirty days, the objection is legally deemed rejected; this is called implicit rejection, and the period for filing a lawsuit begins to run from the day this period expires.

lines: Obligors whose administrative objection is wholly or partly rejected, or deemed implicitly rejected, may file an annulment lawsuit with the Tax Court. The period for filing a lawsuit is 30 days from the date of notification of the rejection decision (and from the date the 30-day response period expires in case of implicit rejection).

lines: Pursuant to the Administrative Procedure Law, lawsuits filed against principal tax amounts automatically halt collection procedures. However, this rule is not absolute for administrative fines: lawsuits filed for the annulment of customs fines may not automatically halt collection. Therefore, for penalties, a “stay of execution” must be separately and explicitly requested in the lawsuit petition, and a concrete demonstration of irreparable harm must be presented to the court.

lines: Before resorting to the administrative objection route, it should be evaluated whether to benefit from the conciliation mechanism in Article 244 of the Customs Law or the fine reduction mechanism in the third paragraph of Article 234. An application for conciliation halts the objection and lawsuit filing periods; however, if conciliation is not reached, an objection must be filed with the Regional Directorate within the remaining period (assuming at least 15 days remain). It is not possible to both seek conciliation and file a lawsuit simultaneously.

lines: If the 15-day objection period is missed, is there no other recourse? No. When the period is missed, the administrative action becomes final; a lawsuit filed directly with the Tax Court at this stage will be dismissed on procedural grounds for lack of merits, on the basis that the “mandatory administrative application route was not exhausted.” Therefore, as soon as the notification is received, tracking of deadlines must begin.

lines: Does filing a lawsuit with the Tax Court automatically halt collection? A lawsuit regarding the principal tax amount automatically halts collection; however, for a lawsuit concerning an administrative fine, this outcome is not automatic. For fines, a request for a stay of execution must also be explicitly stated in the lawsuit petition.

Applying 20 days after the notification of a penalty due to a customs consultancy error can lead to the dismissal of both the administrative objection and the subsequent lawsuit due to period expiration.

lines: Conclusion The legal process against customs duties and administrative fines is an area that intersects fiscal law and foreign trade legislation, requiring high technical knowledge. It is difficult to achieve success with abstract claims against actions of the customs administration based on technical documents such as chemical analysis reports, certificates of origin, and value declaration forms; the defense needs to be supported by international delivery terms and Council of State jurisprudence. Tracking the 15- and 30-day periods from notification is crucial to avoid losing a justified case.

lines: Summary Seizure is a temporary measure applied for evidence security during an investigation; confiscation, on the other hand, is the permanent transfer of ownership to the state by a final court judgment. Goods that are not inherently illegal to possess can be returned to their owner before the end of judicial proceedings by depositing security equal to their full customs value; vehicles used in a crime can be returned by depositing security equal to 25% of their insurance value. Judicial seizures can be appealed to the Criminal Judgeship of Peace within 7 days, and administrative penalties can be appealed to the customs administration within 15 days.

lines: When goods or a vehicle are seized at customs, many people assume it's a permanent loss. However, seizure and confiscation are not the same; seizure is a temporary measure, and the goods or vehicle can be returned to the owner under certain conditions before the conclusion of legal proceedings. Lack of awareness of this distinction causes both individuals and logistics companies to miss deadlines and suffer losses that are difficult to remedy.

lines: Difference Between Seizure and Confiscation
gumrukte-el-konulan-esya-ve-araclarin-ia.text: Difference Between Seizure and Confiscation

lines: Seizure is a temporary measure applied by a court, prosecutor's office, or, in urgent cases, by the customs administration, to ensure the security of evidence during the investigation or prosecution phase; at this stage, ownership does not pass to the state, it is only suspended. Confiscation, on the other hand, is the permanent transfer of ownership of goods and vehicles used in a crime or obtained from a crime to the state by a final judgment of the court at the end of the criminal proceedings.

lines: Recovery of Seized Goods
gumrukte-el-konulan-esya-ve-araclarin-ia.text: Recovery of Seized Goods

lines: Pursuant to Article 10 of Law No. 5607, goods seized as the subject of a smuggling crime are delivered to the custody of the customs administration. Goods whose possession, production, or sale does not constitute a crime in itself (such as textile materials, commercial electronic products, luxury consumer goods) can be returned to their owner if security equal to their customs value is deposited, requested from the judgeship during the investigation phase, or from the court during the prosecution phase. If the defendant is acquitted at the end of the trial, the security is returned as is; in case of conviction, the security is recorded as revenue to the treasury.

If the defendant is acquitted at the end of the trial, the security is returned as is; in case of conviction, the security is recorded as revenue to the treasury.

lines: In contrast, goods whose mere possession constitutes a crime, such as narcotics, smuggled weapons, counterfeit money, or cultural assets whose import is completely prohibited, are not returned to their owner, even with security; these products are subjected to destruction or transfer to public institutions.

lines: Appeal Periods
gumrukte-el-konulan-esya-ve-araclarin-ia.text: Appeal Periods

lines: Strict application periods are stipulated for those who believe their property or vehicle has been unlawfully seized by the customs administration or law enforcement. An appeal against a seizure order issued by a judgeship or applied by the prosecutor's office must be filed with the Criminal Judgeship of Peace with a written petition within 7 days from the date of learning. For administrative fines and seizure decisions issued under Customs Law No. 4458, an administrative appeal must be made to a superior customs officer or the Regional Customs Directorate within 15 days from the date of notification; if this appeal is rejected, a lawsuit must be filed in the Administrative Court.

lines: What happens if the security is not deposited on time? If the security equal to 25% of the insurance value is not deposited within the legal period from the notification of the decision, the customs administration may include the vehicle in the liquidation (sale) procedure. Even if the case is won after the vehicle is liquidated, in-kind return is not possible; only a refund of the value can be obtained.

lines: If I bought the vehicle in good faith, will it still be subject to seizure? Yes, the vehicle itself may be subject to seizure; however, a good faith buyer can get the vehicle back by paying the underpaid taxes and penalties and can claim damages against the seller through a separate recourse lawsuit. lines: Alcohol and Tobacco Seized at Airport Customs: What is the Penalty? Passenger Exemption and Risks under Customs Law No. 4458 Article 235 and Law No. 5607. This guide has been prepared based on the updated customs exemption limits for 2026.

lines: Summary: Passengers aged 18 and over can bring in a maximum of 200 cigarettes (an additional 400 from Duty Free) without tax, 1 liter of alcoholic beverages stronger than 22% by volume, or 2 liters of alcoholic beverages 22% by volume and below. A passenger caught at the Green Lane with quantities exceeding this limit, without commercial intent, will be subject to an administrative fine equal to double the customs tax. If the quantity is commercial in scale or the goods are concealed, the process escalates from an administrative penalty to a smuggling case under Law No. 5607, with a demand for imprisonment ranging from 3 to 6 years.

lines: An extra bottle of alcohol or a carton of cigarettes purchased from Duty Free seems like an innocent purchase for most passengers. However, the outcome is determined not only by the quantity, but also by which corridor is chosen and how the goods are transported. The same excess quantity might result in an administrative fine for one passenger, while for another, it could turn into a lawsuit demanding imprisonment.

lines: 2026 Exemption Limits
havalimani-gumruk-icki-sigara-cezasi-reh.text: 2026 Exemption Limits

lines: Customs legislation strictly defines the amount of tobacco and alcohol that passengers can bring into Turkey without paying duty. These rights are granted only to passengers who are 18 years of age or older.

lines: The exemption limit for cigarettes is a maximum of 200 pieces (1 carton); passengers can purchase an additional 400 cigarettes from arrival Duty Free shops in the customs area after landing at the airport. For other tobacco products, the limit is 50 cigarillos, 20 cigars, or 250 grams of shredded tobacco.

lines: For alcoholic beverages exceeding 22% by volume (such as whiskey, vodka, raki), the exemption limit is a maximum of 1 liter. For beverages 22% by volume and below (such as wine, champagne), the limit is a maximum of 2 liters. Products in the same category cannot be combined; for example, both 1 liter of whiskey and 2 liters of wine cannot be brought in under exemption simultaneously.

lines: Green Lane and Red Lane: Not Just a Corridor Choice
havalimani-gumruk-icki-sigara-cezasi-reh.text: Green Lane and Red Lane: Not Just a Corridor Choice

lines: The two colored corridors encountering passengers at the airport customs exit constitute a legally binding declaration of intent. Passing through the Green Lane means making an official declaration that “I have no products exceeding the legal limit”; only passengers with goods within exemption limits can use this lane. Passengers with goods exceeding the exemption limit or of a commercial nature are obliged to enter the Red Lane and make a declaration to the customs officer.

lines: Sanctions Applied in Case of Limit Overrun

lines: If a passenger is caught passing through the Green Lane with alcohol or tobacco exceeding the exemption limit, and the customs directorate determines there was no intention of smuggling and the goods remain within personal consumption limits, the third paragraph of Article 235 of Customs Law No. 4458 shall apply: an administrative fine equivalent to double the customs duties on the excess goods will be imposed. If the fine is paid, the excess products are handed over to the passenger; if not paid, the products are confiscated and sent for liquidation.

lines: If the seized quantity clearly exceeds personal consumption, is concealed in secret compartments of luggage, or a fraudulent method was used to evade customs control, the event ceases to be an administrative violation and constitutes a crime. In this case, customs officers draw up a crime report and send the file to the Chief Public Prosecutor's Office. Pursuant to Law No. 5607, a public lawsuit demanding imprisonment ranging from 3 to 6 years is filed against persons attempting to bring in alcohol and tobacco without a revenue stamp or subjected to customs procedures; smuggled goods and the vehicles used are confiscated by court order.

lines: Summary: Theft is regulated between articles 141 and 147 of the Turkish Penal Code (TCK) and is subject to very different penalty ranges depending on the manner in which the property is stolen. The penalty for simple theft is 1 to 3 years, while the penalty for qualified forms is 3 to 10 years of imprisonment. In cases of theft committed at night, the penalty is increased by half. Simple and qualified theft are not subject to complaint; even if the victim withdraws the complaint, the case continues as a public prosecution. However, compensation for the damage provides a reduction in the penalty under the provisions of effective remorse.

lines: The first reflex of a person whose property has been stolen is usually to withdraw their complaint when the property is returned. Similarly, a person facing a theft charge believes that if they reach an agreement with the victim, the case will end. However, in Turkish law, most theft crimes are pursued independently of the victim's will. This misconception leads both victims and defendants to face a big surprise during the process.

lines: In its legal definition, theft is the taking of another's movable property without the consent of its possessor, from its location, for the purpose of personal gain or gain for another. For the crime to occur, the property must be movable and the perpetrator must have the intention of obtaining an unjust benefit.

lines: The type of theft committed in situations where the property is unprotected or exposed, without any aggravating factors, is called simple theft. According to Article 141 of the Turkish Penal Code (TCK), the penalty for simple theft is imprisonment from 1 to 3 years. For example, taking a phone left on a table in a cafe without anyone noticing falls within this scope.

lines: If the act of theft is committed in a more dangerous dimension due to the manner of protection of the property, the place where it was committed, the situation of the victim, or the method used, it constitutes qualified theft, and the penalty increases significantly.

While a person who commits theft from a locked house during the day would receive a 6-year sentence, if the same act is committed at 02:00 at night, the penalty increases to 9 years.

lines: Does the Case Drop if the Complaint is Withdrawn?
hirsizlik-sucu-ve-cezasi.text: Does the Case Drop if the Complaint is Withdrawn?

lines: According to the Turkish Penal Code (TCK), neither simple nor qualified theft is subject to complaint. Since these crimes concern public order, they are automatically investigated and prosecuted by the public prosecutor's office. Even if the victim withdraws their complaint at the police station or in court, if it is at the investigation stage, the prosecutor's office continues to file the lawsuit; if it is at the prosecution stage, the court continues the trial and, if the evidence is sufficient, the perpetrator is punished.

Since these crimes concern public order, they are automatically investigated and prosecuted by the public prosecutor's office. Even if the victim withdraws their complaint at the police station or in court, if it is at the investigation stage, the prosecutor's office continues to file the lawsuit; if it is at the prosecution stage, the court continues the trial and, if the evidence is sufficient, the perpetrator is punished.

lines: The fact that withdrawing a complaint does not drop the case does not mean it has no effect. If the perpetrator remedies the damage, meaning the property is returned in kind or its value is paid, this provides a reduction in the penalty under the provisions of effective remorse regulated in Article 168 of the Turkish Penal Code (TCK). If the item or money is returned before the lawsuit is filed, the penalty is reduced by up to two-thirds; if it is returned after the lawsuit is filed but before a decision is made, the penalty is reduced by half.

lines: Firstly, theft for use: taking property not with the intention of possessing it, but to use it for a short time and then return it; for example, taking a friend's car without permission for a spin and then returning it. Secondly, kinship relations: theft committed between spouses not subject to a separation order, siblings living in the same dwelling, uncles, aunts, or nephews and nieces is subject to complaint. However, the law provides for no punishment at all for theft committed between parents, children, or spouses living in the same dwelling.

lines: Summary: Allowing someone else to use a bank account or IBAN information is not an independent crime on its own; however, if the account is used by criminal networks, the account holder is tried as a perpetrator or accomplice of the crime of qualified fraud under Article 158, first paragraph, subparagraph (f) of the Turkish Penal Code and faces imprisonment for 4 to 10 years. The 12th Judicial Package, adopted in 2026, introduced a 50% reduction in punishment for individuals who merely provide their account information to third parties without intent to commit fraud.

lines: Simply giving IBAN information to someone does not constitute a crime on its own. However, when illegal betting, qualified fraud, or money laundering activities are carried out through this account, the account holder becomes central to high criminal proceedings. Three separate legal provisions may come into play:
iban-kullandirma-cezasi-rehberi.text: Simply giving IBAN information to someone does not constitute a crime on its own. However, when illegal betting, qualified fraud, or money laundering activities are carried out through this account, the account holder becomes central to high criminal proceedings. Three separate legal provisions may come into play:

lines: Qualified fraud (TCK Art. 158/1-f): This is fraud committed by using banks and credit institutions as tools. Criminal organizations transfer money obtained from victims not to their own accounts but to rented "custody" accounts. According to the established jurisprudence of the Supreme Court, a person who gives their account to another must foresee that this account may be used in a crime and is considered to have participated in the crime with possible intent. The penalty is 4 to 10 years of imprisonment. Identity concealment (Law No. 5549 Art. 15): A person who allows another to use an account opened in their own name and fails to notify the bank is punished with imprisonment from 6 months to 1 year or a judicial fine. Money laundering of criminal proceeds (TCK Art. 282): Those who mediate transfers knowing or ought to have known that the source of the money in the account is illegal are prosecuted with imprisonment from 3 to 7 years.

lines: A significant legal development occurred in 2026 for the group known as "IBAN victims" in the public, exceeding 50,000 people, the majority of whom are students and citizens with low financial literacy. The 12th Judicial Package, submitted to the Grand National Assembly of Turkey Presidency on June 22, 2026, and accepted by the Justice Commission of the Grand National Assembly of Turkey on June 25, 2026, aims to change the balance of punishment in this area.

lines: In the current practice, the main swindler who personally commits the deception and the person who only provides their account out of goodwill or for a small commission received the same penalty (at least 4 years of imprisonment). With the new regulation, in accordance with the fourth paragraph added to Article 158 of the Turkish Penal Code, the penalty for individuals who are unaware of the fraud mechanism, are not involved in the planning stage of the crime, and whose actual contribution is limited to making their account or card information available to third parties, is reduced by half.

lines: Lifting of Bank Account Block
iban-kullandirma-cezasi-rehberi.text: Lifting of Bank Account Block

lines: The first concrete sanction faced by a person who allows another to use their IBAN is the sudden blocking of their bank accounts. This block can have two different sources: The Financial Crimes Investigation Board (MASAK) imposes a temporary block under Law No. 5549 when it detects unusually rapid money movement in an account; upon a victim's complaint, the Public Prosecutor's Office may request a block decision under Article 128 of the Criminal Procedure Code to seize money obtained from a crime.

lines: I trusted a friend and gave them my IBAN, will I go to jail? If the account is used for fraud or betting purposes, the risk of receiving a penalty is high; the defense "I trusted my friend" is not considered sufficient on its own. However, if it is proven with message records and concrete evidence that there was no intent to commit fraud, the penalty amount can be reduced to a level that will not result in imprisonment by benefiting from the reductions in the 12th Judicial Package.

lines: If I repay the victim, will the case be dropped? Qualified fraud is not a crime contingent on a complaint, so repayment of the damage alone does not drop the case. However, full compensation of the victim's damage triggers effective repentance provisions and provides a significant reduction in punishment up to half; when combined with the reduction in the new judicial package, the penalty can be converted to a judicial fine or suspended.

lines: How to Remove News and Content from the Internet (Blocking Access)? Personality Rights, Privacy, and the Right to Be Forgotten Under Law No. 5651, Articles 9 and 9/A. This guide has been updated as of 2026, based on Law No. 5651 and high court precedents.

lines: Summary: Content removal is the permanent deletion of infringing data from the server, and the legislator considers this the primary method over blocking access. Applications can be made to the Criminal Judgeship of Peace on grounds of infringement of personality rights, privacy, or the right to be forgotten; the judgeship decides within 24 hours at the latest, and positive decisions are implemented via the Association of Access Providers within 4 hours at the latest. A blocking decision may be directed only at the specific link where the infringement occurred, not the entire site.

lines: Everyone who sees negative content about themselves on the internet assumes they can have it removed; however, the law does not make this request limitless. Which content can be removed, which authority to apply to, and how quickly the decision will be implemented are subject to clear rules. A petition prepared without knowing these rules risks both rejection and the possibility of the grievance becoming more visible due to an allegation of "censorship" (Streisand effect).

lines: Difference Between Blocking Access and Content Removal
internetten-icerik-kaldirma-rehberi.text: Difference Between Blocking Access and Content Removal

lines: Blocking access is the restriction of access to the infringing website or relevant URL address only from IP addresses within Turkey; the content is not deleted from the server and can still be viewed with a VPN. Content removal, on the other hand, is the permanent deletion of infringing data from the server and database of the site where it is located. The legislator prioritizes content removal as the method that least harms freedom of expression and press; judgeships primarily decide on content deletion, and if this is not technically possible, they order access blocking.

lines: The cases of unlawfulness required by law are grouped under three main headings.

lines: Infringement of Personality Rights This includes unsubstantiated, defamatory, or false internet publications that damage the honor, dignity, commercial reputation, or integrity of real or legal persons, and is based on Article 9 of Law No. 5651. It is the most frequently used legal remedy. For example, an unsubstantiated news story titled "committing qualified fraud" published about a person who has no ongoing investigation can be the subject of a content removal lawsuit based on the infringement of personality rights.

lines: The Right to Be Forgotten: Can a Correct but Old News Story Also Be Deleted?
internetten-icerik-kaldirma-rehberi.text: The Right to Be Forgotten: Can a Correct but Old News Story Also Be Deleted?

lines: A news story may have been perfectly true and lawful at the time of its publication. However, years later, its continued appearance at the top of search engine results can subject an individual to a constant digital burden due to a past event. According to high court precedents, for content to be removed under the right to be forgotten, the following conditions must be met: a reasonable and long period must have passed since its publication, the news must have lost its topicality and public interest, the person must not be a socially recognized figure, and if the news is based on a judicial case, the person must have been acquitted or completed their sentence.

lines: Two main paths can be followed. The first non-compulsory path is to apply via email or notary public notice through the contact section of the infringing site before resorting to legal action (notice-and-take-down method); the hosting provider is obliged to fulfill legitimate requests. If no result is achieved or the situation is urgent, the aggrieved party applies to the Criminal Judgeship of Peace in their place of residence or where the publication was made, with a petition containing the full URL address of the infringing content and justifications supported by screenshots.

lines: An important technical rule: Criminal Judgeships of Peace, due to freedom of press and expression, cannot issue a wholesale access blocking decision for the main domain name of a news site. The blocking and deletion decision can only be directed at the specific link where the infringement directly occurred.

lines: Implementation of the Decision
internetten-icerik-kaldirma-rehberi.text: Implementation of the Decision

lines: The Criminal Judgeship of Peace examines the application without a hearing, based on documents, and renders a decision within 24 hours at the latest. If the decision is affirmative, the clerk of the judgeship sends the decision to the Association of Access Providers (ESB) for execution. ESB is the umbrella organization to which all internet service providers in Turkey are affiliated and immediately notifies its member service providers and the relevant site of the decision received. Under the law, these decisions must be technically implemented within 4 hours at the latest; severe administrative and judicial sanctions are applied to providers who fail to comply with the deadline.

The objection period is 7 days from the notification of the decision; the objection is examined by the next Criminal Judgeship of Peace in number after the one that made the decision, and the decision rendered is final.

lines: Summary Intentional injury is regulated under articles 86 to 88 of the Turkish Penal Code and is subject to widely varying penalty ranges depending on the severity of the wound, the instrument used, and the identity of the victim. An injury that can be remedied with a simple medical intervention requires imprisonment from 4 months to 1 year or a judicial fine, while severe injury requires imprisonment from 1 year to 3 years.

lines: In cases of injury committed with a weapon, against a spouse, or against a public official, the penalty is increased by half, irrespective of a complaint, and reconciliation is not applied. In cases of injury resulting in permanent disability or death, the penalty increases severalfold.
